title: HTTP-cached catalogs or current PDFs can block new lecture editions

recurrences.environment: Isolated Chromium profile on macOS, actual HTTPS; no service-worker controller, response override or cache clearing
recurrences.actual: The catalog correctly revalidated to v3, while the still-fresh mutable PDF HTTP cache returned the 197313-byte v2. The SHA guard refused that body. A separate fresh profile opened the exact 272394-byte,14-page v3; the immutable5-page v2 restored its existing notebook exactly.
recurrences.expected: Opening the current published edition revalidates its mutable PDF URL and preserves every older edition notebook.
recurrences.confirmed_cause: The current PDF fetch used the default HTTP cache policy. Catalog freshness does not also revalidate a separate PDF request.
recurrences.scope: Current PDF alias revalidation only; immutable edition URLs keep ordinary caching. No PDF bytes, IDs, notebook keys, permissions, authoring or mail schedule change.
